newsitem.title: UK: MEPC says outlook for 1997 encouraging.
newsitem.headline: MEPC says outlook for 1997 encouraging.

text.p: The outlook for 1997 is encouraging as UK rental value growth is becoming more evident with increasing demand for space, said Michael Blakenham, chairman of property company MEPC Plc.
"In the UK, rental value growth is becoming more evident with increasing demand for space," said Blakenham.
He also told shareholders at the company's annual meeting that MEPC had seen an increase in investor activity since its valuation last August.
MEPC said it had made more progress in reshaping its property portfolio by exiting from continental Europe while increasing its presence in the U.S. and Australia.

It has also further reduced the office content of its portfolio in favour of retail, leisure and industrial. The average lot size of its its 449 properties worldwide has now increased to 7.6 million from 4.6 million stg.

Its office porfolio is down to 46 percent from 61 percent, and retail investment now represents 42 percent as against 28 percent. Australia and the U.S. now represent over 30 percent of total group properties compared with 16 percent three years ago.
